title: Aft Fuselage Skin Panel — Corrosion Removal and Protective Restoration
abstract: Corrosion removal and protective restoration on the aft fuselage lower skin panels, the area most affected by galley and lavatory drainage on high-humidity networks.

sections.purpose: This repair removes corrosion from the aft fuselage lower skin panels and restores the protective treatment, without any structural reinforcement.
sections.damage_assessment: Map the corroded area and measure the depth at the deepest point with the pit gauge after the loose product has been removed. This repair is valid for general or pitting corrosion whose clean-up depth does not exceed ten per cent of the local skin thickness, over an area of not more than 150 mm by 150 mm, and where no more than two such areas are present in one skin bay. Exfoliation corrosion of any depth, corrosion at a fastener hole and corrosion under the doubler D5331120951225 are all outside the scope of this repair. Check the stringer D5331123963725 in the same bay before the repair is accepted, because drainage corrosion rarely stops at the skin.
sections.repair_procedure: Get access to the panel from inside the aft fuselage with the lining and any insulation removed locally. Remove the loose corrosion product mechanically and clean the area. Blend out the remaining corrosion with abrasive media, working in stages and checking the depth at each stage; never take more material than the measurement asks for. Do an eddy current inspection of the blended area to confirm that no crack is present under the corroded surface. Feather the blend edges to a slope of not steeper than one in twenty. Measure the remaining thickness with the ultrasonic gauge at five positions and record every reading. Apply chemical conversion coating to the bare metal, then the primer and the topcoat of the standard practice. Where a rivet AES990489-7D has been disturbed, replace it rather than reusing it. Restore the drainage path and confirm that it is clear before the lining goes back.
sections.inspection_requirements: Where the remaining thickness stays above ninety-five per cent of nominal, no repeat inspection is required. Where it is between ninety and ninety-five per cent, do a general visual inspection of the area at every C-check and re-measure the thickness at every six-year check. Report every repair with the thickness readings, so that the fleet trend on drainage corrosion can be maintained. A second blend in the same area is not permitted without an engineering assessment.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: General or pitting corrosion cleaning up within ten per cent of local skin thickness over an area not larger than 150 mm by 150 mm, maximum two areas per skin bay.

repair_drawings.title: Corrosion blend-out and protective restoration, aft fuselage lower skin

type_data.fastener_pattern: Not applicable, no new fastener pattern installed
type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit within the allowable clean-up depth. Thickness re-measurement at every six-year check where the remaining thickness is below ninety-five per cent of nominal.
